assets.mass_policy: The same 0.2 kg mass is applied at every diameter by the fresh evaluator; geometry and candidate controls are frozen from the 100 g experiment. Density varies with volume, not a common real material.

adaptive_selection.method: Measured hand contact points/normals fitted to each finite cylinder; radius, length, surface-normal agreement and opposite contacts are scored. Two best distinct contact families plus a fixed Tip_Pinch reference. Actual success is decided by fresh continuous dynamics, never this geometric rank.
adaptive_selection.limitations: Static side-surface fit excludes joint retargeting, collision, table reachability and actuation. Native init/grasp and gravity-on lift/hold/release tests resolve those limitations. No diameter is declared impossible from this rank.

provenance_accounting.scope: 200 g matched-control re-evaluation only. All stored proposals and all 314 candidate controls are inherited byte-for-byte from the frozen 100 g source pool. No new synthesis, optimization, or controller tuning is performed for 200 g.
provenance_accounting.budget_interpretation: This run changes mass only and repeats the same candidate controls. The uneven 100 g source synthesis budget is historical provenance, not new 200 g optimization or an estimate of maximum 200 g hand capability.

historical_source_synthesis_accounting.scope: Path identities of stored proposals, native optimizer ledger attempts, supplemental variant reruns, and copied valid grasp candidates are separate accounting units. A padded initialization file is not a certified grasp or necessarily a unique numerical pose.
historical_source_synthesis_accounting.budget_interpretation: Reused Tip_Pinch reference scenes retain 50 proposals each, while new main template/diameter jobs normally retain 10 each; tiny fallback jobs retain 5 each. Counts describe this finite uneven search budget, not equal-budget statistical success rates across diameters.

semantics.lift_hold_passed: Final flag: original evaluator lift/hold pass AND sampled five-second-lift protocol gate. LIFT stability uses saved trace samples (normally 10 Hz plus exact phase boundaries); POSTLIFT HOLD uses every 4 ms physics step (250 Hz), including actual rise 95-105 mm throughout 5 s. Neither video replay nor sampled audit observes unsaved lift substeps.
semantics.base_evaluator_outcomes: Frozen original evaluator outcomes are preserved per record before sampled-lift gating; compare them to final flags rather than overwriting their meaning.
semantics.release_passed: Recorded release criterion is evaluated separately; a failed grip that simply leaves the object on the table is not a full-sequence pass.
semantics.full_sequence_passed: base_evaluator full-sequence pass AND sampled-lift stability pass; equivalent to final lift_hold_passed AND release_passed
semantics.representative_videos: Representative selection uses final audited results; the report retains every tested outcome. Video state replay does not compute success.

motion_protocol_audit.scope: Sampled lift gate at recorded trace rate; original every-physics-step postlift hold and release outcomes remain preserved
motion_protocol_audit.downward_tolerance_interpretation: At most 2 mm total retreat from an already reached height during lift (default 2% of 100 mm command). This is an operational monotonicity tolerance, not a universal physical velocity limit.
motion_protocol_audit.dependency_limit: Fingerprint records dependencies at audit time. The evaluator cache itself does not hash referenced scene/mesh/hand files; it must be invalidated if these dependencies change. This fingerprint cannot retroactively prove an earlier unseen asset state.

representative_animations.rendering: Recorded physical-state replay only. No physics is inferred from video or rerun during replay.
representative_animations.selection_policy: All evaluated candidates remain in the results. Each diameter's displayed representative prefers a full-sequence pass after any applied sampled-motion gate, then lift/hold pass, then most satisfied hold and sampled-motion criteria, then smallest normalized worst lift-distance/position/orientation/drawdown error (5 mm final lift, 20 mm tracking/drift, 15 deg orientation, 2 mm lift drawdown tolerances). Input path breaks exact ties.

selected_contact_diagnostics.interpretation: Negative distances quantify compliant MuJoCo contact overlap. Global maxima may arise during released-object floor impact, so grasp/hold and release are separated. Finite overlap remains a simulation-model limitation, especially for tiny objects; no rigidity or real-hardware guarantee is inferred.

matched_load_comparison.design: Matched candidate control targets and identical controller logic. Candidate NPY files are byte-identical; recorded approach/closure/clamp/lift/hold targets are compared at matching physical times. Only runtime object mass is changed. The unchanged release policy computes retreat from measured held-object pose, so its realized retreat direction can differ with load. New success and display choices come from fresh 200 g physics, without new controller tuning or mass-specific synthesis.
matched_load_comparison.control_array_comparison_scope: Approach through end of postlift hold, excluding release. Feedback-dependent release-retreat outputs are intentionally not required to be frame-identical.
matched_load_comparison.pairing: Both input SHA-256 and template/scene/filename suffix must match. The path suffix disambiguates any duplicate numerical payload.
matched_load_comparison.sampling_limit: Lift stability uses the same saved trace sampling and exact boundaries in both loads; postlift-hold gates use every physics step. This comparison adds no observation between saved lift samples.

classification_rules.semantics: Mutually exclusive observed-event categories, ordered by phase; not unique causal diagnoses
classification_rules.initial_contact_shortfall: Fewer than 2 contact points at the end of the 1-second clamp settle; says contact-point shortfall, not number of fingers
classification_rules.no_effective_lift: At least 2 initial points, later lift samples have fewer than 2, and sampled peak rise <20mm
classification_rules.lift_then_contact_loss: At least 2 initial points, sampled peak rise >=20mm and fewer than 2 points later; height traces provide the observed drop evidence
classification_rules.lift_height_precision: Only failed hold criterion is 100±5mm throughout hold and all sampled lift checks pass
classification_rules.numerical_boundary: The original strict 95mm lower bound is preserved; no rounding or new tolerance is applied

evidence_limits: Lift-event timing/peak/contact observations use saved 10Hz states plus phase boundaries; they do not claim exact 250Hz failure onset.
Five-second hold extrema and pass criteria come from evaluator metrics observed every 4ms physics step, not rounded video measurements.
Summed normal contact force alone does not determine tangential friction margin, per-contact forces or resisting torques; no such capacity inference is made.
This comparison reuses frozen controls and changes only object mass, so it is not a new optimized maximum-capacity test of the hand.
